summary:
Build attempt 4 changed only tests/window/PoolWatch.ps1, PoolWatchReportTests.cs and the design record; src is unchanged. I re-ran the 31 PoolWatchReportTests and they pass.

What now holds:
- **Exe runs (O-075):** -Report requires all ten exe runs, five full and five cancelled or closed, with their marks. A crashed or report-less full run, a cancelled run with no report, or a run whose trigger never fired now reads UNDECIDED.
- **Fltmc paste (O-078):** a pasted 'Access is denied' reads FILTERS UNDECIDED.
- **No-link check (O-077):** it runs through Invoke-NoLinkWalk's own flags at three levels, with a detector that sees a followed link, and -Protocol refuses to start on a false prepare.json.
- **Settle gate (O-076):** the gate exists, but its threshold does not do what it was added for.

I fed -Report hand-built run logs and found two defects.

1. **Settle gate too loose (major).** The gate passes a boot once two 60-second gaps each move less than 16 MiB. The drift VOID rule fires once I0's drift is more than 3x I1's; at spike 3's idle drift of 11,000 B/s that is about 2 MiB a minute.
   - A boot that passes the gate on two 10 MiB gaps and keeps growing 2 or 5 MiB a minute through I0 still ends 'OUTCOME VOID' (I0 45,953 or 98,381 B/s against 11,000).
   - The 16 MiB figure was my own suggestion in round 2, so this corrects my earlier fix as well as the build.
2. **Guard stop on S or P reads UNDECIDED (minor).** When the guard kills ScanArm S or P, it prints no summary line. -Report then says 'UNDECIDED: arm S or L's file count is missing' before its new guard-stop clause runs.
   - That contradicts the design record ('an arm the guard stopped (L, S, P or an exe run) counts as over T').
   - The 'probe-guard-stop' row passes only because it gives the stopped S arm a summary of 50,000 opens, which a killed process never writes.

My scratch folders are removed.

Second round: Second round on build attempt 4 found one new defect: -Report can read PASS when a cancel or close run never actually stopped.

-Report decides whether one of the five cancelled or closed runs actually stopped by matching a single phrase from the window hook's log ('ended before the trigger'), stored as ranFull. The hook logs two other ways of never acting:
- 'the app shut down before the trigger';
- 'the trigger … was not met within N s'.

Both leave ranFull false, so the run is counted as cancelled or closed. I fed -Report hand-built run logs:
- **X4 (close):** the app crashed before its trigger, with no report. Read A/PASS.
- **X2 (cancel):** its deadline passed and the scan ran to Completed. Read A/PASS.

So the O-075 rule that a run whose trigger never fired is not one of the five holds for only one of the hook's three never-acted outcomes.

Nothing else I tried broke. That covered:
- the new fltmc list matcher;
- Test-Settled and Wait-Settle;
- Test-NoLinkWalker's robocopy calls and its cleanup;
- the -Protocol refusal;
- the exe-run count and exit checks.

My scratch folder is removed.

findings.claim:
The settle gate added for R2-N1 does not prevent the VOID it was added for.

Wait-Settle and Test-Settled treat the boot as settled once two consecutive 60-second settle gaps each move both pools by less than SettleStepBytes = 16 MiB, i.e. up to about 279,000 B/s. -Report then VOIDs the run when I0's drift is more than 3x I1's (`$hi -gt $Tolerance.DriftDisagree * [Math]::Max($lo, $noise)`). At spike 3's measured post-settle drift of 10,936 B/s, that VOID fires above about 33,000 B/s, roughly 1.9 MiB a minute. So any boot whose growth has slowed to between about 2 and 16 MiB a minute when the gate opens starts I0, L, S, P and the ten exe scans, and -Report VOIDs the whole ~4-hour post-Restart session at the end. That is the R2-N1 failure, only in a narrower band.

Spike 3's own settle reached the gate with a last gap of 5.6 MiB. It happened to calm afterwards, to an I0 drift of 0.63 MiB a minute, but nothing in the protocol waits for that.

I proposed the 16 MiB figure myself in round 2, taken from spike 3's V2 limit without checking it against the drift rule.
findings.evidence: tests/window/PoolWatch.ps1:81 (SettleStepBytes = 16MB), :467-477 Wait-Settle, :590-602 Test-Settled, :657-660 (drift-disagreement VOID). Measured with hand-built run logs through `PoolWatch.ps1 -Report -NoWrite`: settle marks of 10 gaps at 85 MiB then 2 gaps at 10 MiB (the gate passes), I1 at 11,000 B/s. With I0 then flat the run reads A/PASS. With I0 at 2 MiB/min it reads 'OUTCOME VOID: idle drift of pagedBytes disagrees between I0 (45,953 B/s) and I1 (11,000 B/s), over 3x'. At 5 MiB/min it reads VOID (98,381 B/s).
findings.fix: Make the gate as strict as the VOID rule it protects: SettleStepBytes about 2 MiB per 60-second gap, i.e. DriftDisagree x spike 3's 10,936 B/s x MarkEverySec, rounded. Keep the 30-minute cap and the early stop, which fails in minutes instead of after 4 hours. Alternatively, have -Protocol check I0's own first-half against second-half drift before starting L, and extend I0 rather than proceed when they differ by more than DriftDisagree. Add a PoolWatchReportTests row in which the gate passes on 10 MiB gaps and I0 still grows 2 MiB/min, pinning whichever behaviour is chosen. Update the tolerance row text and the R2-N1 record, which both say 16 MiB.

findings.claim:
A guard stop on arm S or P does not count as over T in practice. It reads UNDECIDED.

ScanArm prints its one JSON summary only after its loop (Program.cs Probe/Plain `Print(...)` at the end). When the guard kills it (Invoke-Arm `$p.Kill()`), stdout is empty and the arm line's `summary` is null. -Report's projection loop then returns 'UNDECIDED: arm S or L's file count is missing' (PoolWatch.ps1:765), before the new `[bool]$armBy['S'].guardStop` clause at :773 can route to B. That contradicts two statements:
- the design record's tolerance row (docs/design/SL-095-container-layer-store.md:112, 'An arm the guard stopped (L, S, P or an exe run) counts as over T');
- the builder's O-075 claim that OverArm covers S and P.

The 'probe-guard-stop' row in TheReportRoutesARunAsTheToleranceRowSays, and its reason in ExeRunsThatAreMissingCrashedOrStoppedByTheGuardNeverPass, are green only because the test builder gives the guard-stopped S arm a summary (`opened 50,000`) that a killed ScanArm never writes. The real shape, a null summary, is not fed.

The consequence is the safe direction (UNDECIDED, never PASS). But the session in which SizeProbe's per-file opens blow the guard, the strongest evidence for outcome B, decides nothing.
findings.evidence: tests/window/PoolWatch.ps1:765 (UNDECIDED when `$line.summary` is null) before :773-775 (guardStop gives sOver, then B); PoolWatch.ps1 Invoke-Arm (summary read from stdout's last JSON line, null after Kill); tests/window/ScanArm/Program.cs Probe/Plain (Print only after the loop); tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/PoolWatchReportTests.cs Build(): `Arm("S", "probe", summary: new() { ["opened"] = 50_000L, ... }, guardStop: scenario == "probe-guard-stop" ? guard : null)`. Measured: the same run with S killed by the guard and summary null reads 'OUTCOME UNDECIDED / REASON UNDECIDED: arm S or L's file count is missing'; P killed reads the same for P.
findings.fix: In the S/P projection loop, when the arm's guardStop is set, skip the summary and projection and mark it over T. S stopped while P projects within T, or P is also stopped, gives B (or C by the excess rule, using 'stopped' for both). Change the probe-guard-stop row to give S a null summary, as a killed ScanArm leaves it.

findings.claim:
-Report counts an exe-cancel or exe-close arm as one of DONE (c)'s five cancelled runs unless `ranFull` is true. Invoke-ExeArm sets ranFull only when the hook log matches 'ended before the trigger' (PoolWatch.ps1 Invoke-ExeArm, `$line['ranFull'] = [bool](@($acted) -match 'ended before the trigger')`).

The window hook has two other outcomes in which it never presses Cancel or closes the window (tests/window/FsaWindowHook/StartupHook.cs:653 and :665):
- 'refused mode=… reason=the app shut down before the trigger';
- 'refused mode=… reason=the trigger … was not met within N s'.

In both, ranFull stays false and the arm passes Get-Verdict's checks (:706-720):
- An exe-close arm needs no report, so an app that crashed before its close trigger counts as a closed run.
- An exe-cancel arm whose deadline passed while the scan ran to the end has a report (status Completed), which is all :717 asks for.

Nothing compares a cancel arm's report status with 'Cancelled', and nothing requires an 'acted' line or a foldersAtCancel value. So a session in which one of the five cancel/close runs crashed, or never cancelled, can read A/PASS for DONE (c).
findings.evidence:
Measured by feeding `PoolWatch.ps1 -Report -NoWrite` hand-built run logs that are otherwise clean, each with settle marks, ten exe runs and an armable control:
- X4 (exe-close) with exitCode -532462766, report null, ranFull false, hookLog ['refused mode=close reason=the app shut down before the trigger'] and foldersAtCancel null gave 'OUTCOME A / VERDICT PASS'.
- X2 (exe-cancel) with exit 0, report status Completed, ranFull false and hookLog ['refused mode=stop reason=the trigger past=C:\Users pastfolders=1000 was not met within 3,600 s'] also gave 'OUTCOME A / VERDICT PASS'.
Code: tests/window/PoolWatch.ps1:717 (only a null report is caught for exe-cancel; exe-close not at all) and :719-720 (only ranFull).
findings.fix:
In Invoke-ExeArm, record `acted = [bool](@($acted) -match '^acted ')`; foldersAtCancel is already null exactly when no 'acted' line exists. In Get-Verdict's ten-run check, return UNDECIDED, naming the arm and the hook's refused line, for any of these:
- an exe-cancel or exe-close arm that did not act;
- an exe-cancel arm whose report.status is not 'Cancelled'.
Add rows 'close-app-shut-down-before-trigger' and 'cancel-trigger-deadline' to TheReportRoutesARunAsTheToleranceRowSays.

obligations.evidence: PoolWatch.ps1:467-477 Wait-Settle runs between R0 and I0 (:984-987), stops at SettleCapSec (:82), and -Report re-checks with Test-Settled (:636-642). It implements the 16 MiB rule exactly as the obligation asked. That threshold does not keep I0 out of the drift VOID; see R3-1.

Test-FltmcList (PoolWatch.ps1:350-355) requires the 'Filter Name  Num Instances' header and no '0x8007|Access is denied|failed'. Read-FltmcPaste feeds Get-EnvironmentRecord, and Get-FiltersLine applies the same test to fltmc.txt and to environment records. The refused-paste cases in MissingOrNullReadingsAreUndecidedAndABurstGapIsLeftOutOfDrift pass.

drift:
Two statements now read wrong:
- The design record's tolerance row says a guard-stopped S or P arm counts as over T; in the code it reads UNDECIDED (R3-2).
- PoolWatch.ps1's header line for -Environment still says fltmc.txt 'is appended'. A refused paste is now recorded as 'not a filter list: …' instead.

Nothing new departed from the design in this round. R3-3 contradicts the builder's own declared departure for O-075: 'a cancelled or closed run whose hook trigger never fired … does not count as one of the 5'. The code implements that for only one of the hook's three never-fired outcomes.
